title: Vertical Positioning Microlearning
summary: A sales-enablement microlearning case study built as one Rise module with distinct seaport and airport components, a shared learning architecture, scenario practice, selective multimedia, and specialist review.

content.business_need: Help sellers build usable context for two industry settings without creating separate trainings or flattening the two environments into one generic vertical story.
content.audience: Internal sellers and channel partners who need concise industry context before discovery and positioning conversations.
learning_objectives: Recognize the operating context and common priorities within the seaport and airport settings.
Connect customer needs to relevant solution use cases at a sales-ready level.
Practice making a customer-facing decision in a short scenario.
Locate supporting resources for deeper follow-up instead of overloading the module.
content.role: Instructional designer and developer responsible for content scoping, learning architecture, Rise build, scenario design, multimedia integration, and review coordination.
content.design_approach: Built one Rise module around a repeatable Context → Use Cases → Practice → Resources pattern. The learner rhythm stays consistent while the customer priorities, examples, and scenario judgment change by vertical.
content.development_process: Scoped approved source material, structured distinct seaport and airport components, built the module in Rise 360, used a short Colossyan presenter segment where narration improved orientation, and coordinated internal QA and specialist review through Review 360 and Asana.
outcomes: Delivered one focused Rise module with distinct seaport and airport components.
Used a consistent learning pattern that reduced navigation friction without treating the two verticals as interchangeable.
Kept deeper reference material outside the core microlearning so the experience remained concise and maintainable.

source_material_notes: Generalized from documented industry-focused sales enablement work. Industry-specific proprietary messaging, internal screenshots, customer details, reviewer comments, dates, links, and source material are intentionally omitted.
